origin.description: Store a package database for a repository and package type, and return the cached database.

arguments.name: repos
arguments.text: Character vector, the base URL(s) of the repositories to use. Names are part of the cache key, so a named vector and an unnamed vector do not share an entry.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: Character string giving the package type, such as "source". It is part of the cache key and is not interpreted. Names on this string are part of the key. A factor would be a different key.

arguments.name: db
arguments.text: The package database to store when this repository and type are not already cached.

origin.details: The cache key is serialize(list(repos, type), ascii = TRUE), so the values and the names both matter. If that pair is already stored, the previous database is returned and db is ignored. A stored NULL is replaced on the next call, because the test is is.null and a missing binding is NULL too. The manual page has no example line for this function.
origin.value: The cached database. On the first call for a pair, this is db. On a later call, this is the database stored by the first call.
origin.example:
available_packages_reset()
first <- available_packages_set("https://cran.r-project.org", "source", c(Package = "digest"))
second <- available_packages_set("https://cran.r-project.org", "source", c(Package = "digest", Version = "9"))
cat(paste0("after reset, set(\"https://cran.r-project.org\", \"source\", c(Package = \"digest\")) returns ", first[["Package"]], ", and a second set with Version 9 still returns ", second[["Package"]], ".\n"))

translation.description: Store a package database for a repository and package type, and return the cached database.

arguments.name: repos
arguments.text: A string, a list of strings, or a dict of names to URLs. A string or a list is an unnamed character vector. A dict is a named vector, and its keys are the names. Names are part of the cache key.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: A string such as "source", or a dict when that string has a name. It is part of the cache key and is not interpreted. The check uses a plain string.

arguments.name: db
arguments.text: The database to store when this repository and type are not already cached. A dict is a named character vector.

translation.details: The cache key is the values and the names of repos and type. A named repository vector and an unnamed one do not share an entry. If that pair is already stored, the previous database is returned and db is ignored. A stored None is replaced on the next call, matching is.null. The manual page has no example line for this function.
translation.value: The cached database. On the first call for a pair, this is db. On a later call, this is the database stored by the first call.
translation.example:
from remotes.available_packages import available_packages_reset, available_packages_set
available_packages_reset()
first = available_packages_set("https://cran.r-project.org", "source", {"Package": "digest"})
second = available_packages_set("https://cran.r-project.org", "source", {"Package": "digest", "Version": "9"})
print("after reset, set(\"https://cran.r-project.org\", \"source\", c(Package = \"digest\")) returns " + first["Package"] + ", and a second set with Version 9 still returns " + second["Package"] + ".")
